title: 2D Vector Addition and Dot Product
spec: Write a module for 2D vector math. Implement `add_vectors(v1, v2)` where both arguments are tuples of two floats, unpacking them to compute their sum, and returning a new tuple. Implement `dot_product(v1, v2)` which similarly unpacks the tuples and returns the scalar dot product. Implement `scale_vector(v, factor)` which unpacks a single vector and multiplies both components by the factor. In the `main` block, define `v_a` as `(3.0, 4.0)` and `v_b` as `(1.0, 2.0)`. Call `add_vectors` with these variables, store the result in `sum_v`, and print `sum_v`. Then do the same for `dot_product`, storing and printing the scalar result.

title: Rectangle Area and Scaling
spec: Write a module for rectangle geometry. Implement `compute_area(width, height)` which returns the computed area. Implement `compute_perimeter(width, height)` which returns the perimeter. Implement `create_rectangle(width, height)` that simply returns the two arguments as a tuple. Implement `scale_rectangle(rect_tuple, factor)` which unpacks a `(width, height)` tuple, multiplies each dimension by the factor, and returns a new `(new_width, new_height)` tuple. In the driver block, define `width = 10` and `height = 20`. Pass them to `compute_area` and store the result. Then call `create_rectangle` to build a tuple `r = (10, 20)`, pass it to `scale_rectangle` with a factor of 2, store the resulting tuple in `scaled_rect`, and print it.

title: Time Interval Intersection
spec: Write a module to compute the intersection of 1D time intervals. Implement `intersect_intervals(i1, i2)`, where each interval is a tuple of a start and end time. Unpack them and use the built-in `max` and `min` functions to find the overlap; if the overlap is valid (start strictly less than end), return it as a tuple, else return None. Implement `merge_intervals(i1, i2)` which returns the bounding interval of both (minimum start, maximum end) as a tuple. Write a main block that defines `i_a = (10, 20)` and `i_b = (15, 25)`. Call the intersect function on them, store the result in a variable, and print it directly.

title: Key-Value Configuration Parsing
spec: Write a script that processes configuration lines. Implement `parse_line(line, fallback)` that splits a string by the equals sign (without passing a maxsplit argument). Unpack the split result into `key` and `value` on a single line, returning them as a tuple; if it fails due to unpacking an invalid number of items, catch the exception and return `(line, fallback)`. Implement `apply_setting(config_dict, pair_tuple)` which unpacks a `(key, value)` tuple and assigns it into the dictionary. Implement `get_setting(config_dict, key)` that returns the value. In the main function, initialize an empty dictionary, process the string `"port=8080"` passing `False` as the fallback, store the returned tuple, apply it to the dictionary, and print the dictionary.

title: List Pagination Helper
spec: Write a pagination module. Implement `get_bounds(page, page_size)` which calculates the zero-based start index and the limit, returning them as a tuple `(offset, limit)`. Implement `slice_items(items, bounds)` where `bounds` is that tuple; unpack it, compute the end index, and return the sliced list. Implement `get_total_pages(total_items, page_size)` which calculates the total pages using standard integer arithmetic. Finally, implement `create_page_response(items, total_pages)` which returns a dictionary with these two arguments mapped to string keys. In the driver code, generate a list of items, compute bounds for page 3 with size 10, storing it in `b_tuple`, pass it to `slice_items`, and print the result.

title: Text Normalization and Substitution
spec: Write a text normalization utility. Implement `normalize_spacing(text, max_iters)` which uses `text.replace("  ", " ")` repeatedly up to `max_iters` times to remove double spaces. Implement `create_pair(word1, word2)` which simply returns them as a tuple. Implement `apply_substitutions(text, subs)` where `subs` is a list of tuples. Iterate through it using `for old, new in subs:` and apply each substitution using the string `replace` method. In the main block, create an empty list named `subs`. Append the result of `create_pair("foo", "bar")` to it, then append `create_pair("baz", "qux")` on the next line. Call `apply_substitutions` on a test string with `subs` and print the result.

title: Undirected Graph Adjacency
spec: Write an undirected graph module using adjacency lists. Implement `add_edge(graph, edge_tuple)` where `edge_tuple` is a tuple of two node names. Unpack it and append each node to the other's list in the graph dictionary. Implement `check_adjacent(graph, edge_tuple)` which unpacks the tuple and returns True if the two nodes are directly connected in the graph. Include a driver that initializes an empty graph dictionary with empty lists for keys "A", "B", and "C". Define `edge1 = ("A", "B")`, pass it to `add_edge`, then do the same for `edge2 = ("B", "C")`. Finally, define a tuple for "A" and "C" and print the result of checking their adjacency.

title: File Path Splitting and Joining
spec: Write a file path utility. Import `os` and `sys` on the same line. Implement `split_path(path)` which calls `os.path.split(path)` to get the directory and filename, unpacks them on one line, then calls `os.path.splitext` on the filename to separate the name and extension, unpacks those, and returns a tuple of `(directory, extension)`. Implement `join_custom(dir_path, filename)` which safely joins the two arguments using `os.path.join`. Implement `get_fallback_ext(path, default_ext)` which calls `split_path`, ignores the directory, and returns a tuple of `(path, extension)` or `(path, default_ext)` if empty. Include a driver block that calls `join_custom` on `"/var/log"` and `"system.log"`, and prints the result.

title: Cartesian to Polar Conversions
spec: Write a module to convert between 2D coordinate systems. Import `math` and `cmath` on a single line. Implement `to_polar(x, y)` which uses `math.hypot(x, y)` for the radius and `math.atan2(y, x)` for the angle, returning them as a tuple. Implement `to_cartesian(r, theta)` which computes x and y using `math.cos` and `math.sin` multiplied by the radius, and returns `(x, y)`. Implement `distance(p1, p2)` where each is an `(x, y)` tuple; unpack them and use `math.hypot` to return the Euclidean distance. Write a main section that passes `3.0` and `4.0` into the polar function, stores the returned tuple in a variable `p_tuple`, and prints `p_tuple`.

title: Safe Dictionary Merging
spec: Write a dictionary utility script. Implement `merge_dicts(dict_a, dict_b)` that iterates over the key-value items of the second dictionary using a for loop, assigning each into the first dictionary, and returns the modified first dictionary. Implement `safe_get_list(target_dict, key)` which uses the dictionary `get(key, default)` method to return the existing list or an empty list if the key is not found. Implement `clone_dict(source_dict, default_val)` which iterates over the source dictionary and populates a new dictionary where all values are replaced by the default. In the driver, define `d1 = dict(a=1, b=2)` and on the next line `d2 = dict(c=3, d=4)`. Call `merge_dicts` with both dictionaries, store the result, and print it.

title: Linear Range Mapping
spec: Write a utility for linear value mapping. Implement `map_linear(value, range_pair)` where `range_pair` is a tuple containing two tuples: an input range and an output range. Unpack the pair into `in_range` and `out_range`. On subsequent lines, unpack `in_range` into min and max, and do the same for `out_range`. Compute the proportional ratio of the value within the input bounds, then apply it to the output range. Implement `clamp_value(value, limits)` which unpacks the limits tuple, computes the minimum of the value and the upper limit on one line, and then returns the maximum of the lower limit and that result on the next line. In main, create `in_r = (0, 10)` and `out_r = (0, 100)`. Combine them as `ranges = (in_r, out_r)`. Map the value 5 and print the result.

title: Complex Number Arithmetic
spec: Write a module for complex number arithmetic using tuples. Implement `add_complex(c1, c2)` where each argument is a `(real, imag)` tuple. Unpack both arguments on separate lines, compute their sum, and return a new tuple. Implement `multiply_complex(c1, c2)` which similarly unpacks both tuples on separate lines, computes the complex product (real*real - imag*imag for the real part, etc.), and returns it as a `(real, imag)` tuple. Implement `conjugate_complex(c)` which unpacks the single tuple and returns a new tuple with the imaginary part negated. In the driver block, define `c_a = (1.0, 2.0)` and `c_b = (3.0, 4.0)`. Call `multiply_complex` with them, store the result in a variable, and print it.

title: Matrix Dimensions and Transposition
spec: Write a matrix utility module. Implement `get_dimensions(matrix, default_cols)` which calculates the number of rows and columns, returning them as a tuple. Implement `create_empty(rows, cols)` which generates a 2D list of zeros using the given sizes. Implement `flatten_matrix(matrix, dims_tuple)` which unpacks the `(rows, cols)` tuple on one line and iterates through the matrix to return a single flat list. Implement `transpose_dimensions(dims_tuple)` which unpacks the dimensions and returns them reversed as a tuple. In the driver, call `create_empty(2, 3)`, store it, get its dimensions by calling `get_dimensions`, store that tuple, pass it to `transpose_dimensions`, and print the transposed tuple.
